belief: I'll always be the odd one out.
origins: A lifetime of being the one who looks, moves, or sounds different can create the expectation that groups will never fully include us.
teaches: “God settles the lonely in families.” “From Him the whole body, fitted and held together by every supporting ligament, grows and builds itself up in love through the work of each individual part.” “Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.” God’s family includes people of every kind, and the body needs your part. Some groups are not welcoming, but others are. You do not have to be the same to belong.
self_statements: Groups will always push me out.
errors: Believing I either fit perfectly or am an outsider.
Feeling different and concluding I do not belong.
questions: Where have I felt included, even once?
What gift do I bring that others do not?
What does Scripture say about the body?
truth: I belong to God’s family, and the body needs me as I am. I can look for welcoming groups, bring my gifts, and make room for others who feel different.
hw_truths: God settles the lonely in families.
I have a gift for the common good.
There is no division in Christ.
I can make room for others.
log: Each week, note one welcoming moment.
actions: Include someone who looks left out.
prayer: Father, I feel like the odd one out. Place me in a family where I belong, use my gifts, and help me welcome others. Amen.
hw_questions: Where have I felt included, even once?
What gift do I bring that others do not?
What does Scripture say about the body?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Every part of the body is needed, including me.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I'll always be the odd one out.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
